recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the community wants to revisit Object.equals()/hashCode(), open or handle a Java implementation issue in hapifhir/org.hl7.fhir.core with compatibility review.
issue_request: FHIR-5656 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 FHIR-core change request asking the Java reference implementation to make Extension, Type, Element, Base, and related classes comparable. Jira discussion rejected overriding Object.equals()/hashCode() and chose explicit deep and shallow equality methods instead.
initial_application: Historical commit e7b24dac064ae69bf393785eb025dd151b069061 added equalsDeep(), equalsShallow(), and comparison helpers to Base and generated overrides for Element, Extension, and ElementDefinition. The commit message does not mention FHIR-5656, but the date, title, touched classes, and Jira comment saying explicit methods were added match the issue resolution.
additional_context: The current HL7/fhir source tree contains no Java model classes or tools/java implementation source. Current Java model source is maintained in hapifhir/org.hl7.fhir.core, where Base still defines equalsDeep()/equalsShallow() and generated classes such as Element and Extension override explicit equality methods. Later Zulip discussions revisited Object.equals()/hashCode() overrides but identified ambiguity and compatibility risks rather than a current spec-source change.
reconciliation: No HL7/fhir source files were changed. The issue's implemented behavior is in the Java implementation lineage, and any future change to Java model equality belongs in the external Java core repository rather than this spec checkout.
